title: Launch Window Playbook — KPI Orbit & Tactical Checklist
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a hands-on playbook for managing a bounded launch window (the 'orbit') for feature launches where we must control traffic, observe KPI drift, and trigger staged fallback policies automatically. It combines a lightweight KPI tracker, an owner map, an operational checklist for go/no‑go gates, and runbook snippets for quick escalation.

Scope:
- Target launches: cross-functional product features that require staged traffic (hosted API releases, console changes with infra impact, Dedicated capacity defaults)
- Not for: fully internal experiments, infra-only patches w/o customer impact

Definitions (quick):
- Orbit: the planned window + phased traffic ramp (0% -> 100%) for a launch
- Burn rate: incremental tokens or requests per minute compared to baseline
- Canary: first 1-5% of traffic routed to new model/config variant
- KPI anchor: the primary metric used to judge launch health (latency, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, model quality score)

KPI ORBIT TRACKER (single-line CSV format for quick paste into sheets)
phase,start_date,end_date,traffic_pct,primary_kpi,alert_threshold,owner
canary,2026-03-20,2026-03-20,1,99th_latency_ms,>600,Maya Patel
early_bump,2026-03-21,2026-03-22,10,error_rate_pct,>1.2,Diego Alvarez
ramp,2026-03-23,2026-03-29,50,quality_eval_pass_pct,<85,Ruth Kim
full,2026-03-30,2026-04-06,100,cost_per_1k_tokens,>1.35,Samir Gupta

Quick note: keep the CSV header row when copying into the product-ops KPI sheet and link to the launch-conductor ticket.

Pre-launch essentials (owner, ticket, accept criteria) — checklist style:
- Product spec finalized + linked PR (owner: Product) — ticket PROJ-4921 — must include success scenarios and SLOs.
- Model/Config pinned (owner: Applied ML) — quantization/variant documented — integration test green.
- Infra capacity reservation (owner: Platform Eng) — Dedicated pools reserved and autoscale guardrails configured.
- Monitoring hooks (owner: Observability) — dashboards for token-level cost, 99th latency, error rate; synthetic prompts for quality checks.
- Rollback plan & fallback variants (owner: Serving Runtime) — kernel-compat fallback and smaller model variant available.
- Customer comms draft (owner: GTM) — beta cohort notice + support triage channel set.

Go / No‑Go Gate Snapshot (to be completed in a meeting 24h before start):
- All blockers resolved (yes/no)
- Synthetic quality eval passing at baseline thresholds (yes/no)
- Infra autoscale smoke test (yes/no)
- Playbook & on-call assigned (yes/no)
- Rollback validated end-to-end (yes/no)
If any answer is NO => action owner to provide remediation plan + push window.

Phase run instructions (canary -> early_bump -> ramp -> full):
- Canary (1%): route small traffic; collect immediate telemetry for 10 minutes; if 99th latency > threshold or error rate > threshold, trigger immediate rollback and tag incident; else continue 60m.
- Early bump (10%): validate user-visible quality via synthetic eval set and 6 customer support checks; if quality_eval_pass_pct dips below threshold or cost per 1k tokens spikes > 1.5x expected, pause ramp and initiate triage.
- Ramp (50%): maintain close coordination with Platform Eng for autoscale; incrementally increase traffic over 6–12 hours with health checks every 30 minutes.
- Full (100%): monitor for 48 hours continuously for regression signals in model quality and cost.

Automated alerting thresholds (examples):
- 99th latency: alert if >600ms sustained for 5m
- Error rate: alert if >1% for 3m or 2x baseline
- Quality eval (automated synthetic set): alert if drop >8 percentage points vs baseline
- Cost per 1k tokens: alert on >25% uplift vs forecast for 30m
- SLO burn-rate: if burn rate is >2x forecast, open ops incident and cap traffic at previous stable checkpoint.

Fallback taxonomy (ordered):
1) Soft degrade: reduce feature-specific sampling (immediately reversible)
2) Model fallback: route to quantized or smaller variant (needs config switch)
3) Regional fallback: shift traffic to alternate region with spare capacity
4) Full rollback: revert to previous release; inform GTM + CS; open post-mortem

Escalation playbook (who to ping):
- Primary owner (phase owner) -> #launch-ops Slack
- If incident persists 15m -> On-call SRE -> #sre-oncall
- If customer-impacting or SLA breach -> Head of Product Ops (Lena Park) + Legal & Security as needed

Runbook snippets (copy-paste examples):
- Rollback command: /infra/ops rollback --release=<tag> --verify=smoke
- Temporarily cap traffic: /router/ops set-rate --route=<route> --pct=<value>
- Switch to fallback model: /models/switch --route=<route> --variant=quantized-small

Post-launch 7-day hygiene checklist:
- 24–72h: validate adoption and key signals; collect any false positive alerts and tune thresholds.
- Day 3: review cost drift and adjust batching/quantization recommendations.
- Day 7: run a quality sweep vs holdout prompts; decision: keep, iterate, or rollback.
- Post-mortem due within 5 business days if any gate breached.

Owner matrix (single-line for quick import):
area,owner,slack,backup
observability,Diego Alvarez,#obs-diego,Lena Park
serving_runtime,Samir Gupta,#runtime-team,Diego Alvarez
product_owner,Maya Patel,#prod-maya,Ruth Kim
platform_eng,Lena Park,#platform-oncall,Samir Gupta
customer_success,Ruth Kim,#cs-betas,#cs-oncall

Notes + open questions (work-in-progress):
- Should we add a budget gate that auto-pauses at $X/day spend? (action: finance + product-ops to propose thresholds)
- What’s the canonical synthetic prompt set for quality_eval_pass_pct? (action: Applied ML to publish)
- Consider adding a lightweight canary UX observation: 3 customer support triage checks vs synthetic only.

Appendix: useful links
- Launch conductor ticket: PROJ-4921
- Canary deploy tutorial: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Canary+Deploys
- Postmortem template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Postmortem+Template

Bottom line: use this playbook as the live checklist when you need predictable, observable, and reversible launches. Copy the CSV sections into the product-ops tracker, populate owners, and confirm the go/no-go snapshot 24 hours in advance.

End of doc.
